messages:
maria: Quick check-in: preparing stricter isolation for EU/APAC private clusters. Requirements: deny-by-default netpols, explicit KMS/HSM proxy allowlist, tamper-evident audit chain, and scoped RBAC for keystore proxies. I want a minimal blast-radius plan before we flip the switch.
sanjay: I'll draft the netpol baseline today. thinking: an enforced egress proxy pattern (all pods -> envoy-forwarder -> egress) + `NetworkPolicy` denyAll by default. this makes allow-lists tiny.
elliot: RBAC constraints: create a namespaced Role for keystore-proxy with only `keystore.redwood.io:decrypt` and `get` on keymeta. bind only to the infra SA. no ClusterRoleBindings. also add OA token restrictions: `aud` + `iss` checks.
dina: KMS notes: HSM cluster has leader election windows ~6s, leader promotion sometimes causes short auth failures. need client retry logic + healthcheck-based endpoint failover. also require mTLS from proxy to HSM, and mutual cert pinning for extra assurance.
maria: Good. For audits: EU customers need 1yr retention and WORM guarantees. propose: append-only audit file with HMAC chain per entry (prev_hash included). store the chain in remote SIEM over private peering. That makes tamper attempts obvious.
jen: Compliance thumbs-up on HMAC chain + peering, but we must include clock-sync verification and enforce monotonic sequence numbers to avoid reorder attacks. logs should include signed sequence id and signer SAN.
thomas: Incident flow: if client detects >3 consecutive 403s from HSM within 15s, switch to degraded-mode: serve reads from sealed cache (no decrypts) and emit `keystore.degraded` metric. Runbook: page sec-oncall, attempt 3 endpoint switches over 2 minutes, then failover to DR HSM and rotate limited audit token.
ryan: About bastion removal: ops wants bastionless clusters, but we must ensure admin access goes through k8s-proxy with mTLS + short-lived certs issued by our CA. Removing jumpboxes without that increases risk. recommend phased removal after proxy rollout.
sanjay: Netpol snippet for canary I want to run:`apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: private-deny-eu-canary
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress: []`Followed by narrow allows like:`- to:
  - podSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: envoy-forwarder
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443`
maria: Nice — run canary on eu-staging with `canary=true` label. ops-bot, kick it off and report failures by type (egress/ingress/deny).
ops-bot: canary:netpol-eu started by <@maria> on eu-staging. 10 pods evaluated. 3 pods failed egress: 2 telemetry exporters, 1 legacy packagemanager. details: https://ci.internal/canary/4071234567 :warning:
dina: Telemetry exporters must route via `envoy-forwarder`. we'll update sidecar config in the next PR. legacy packagemanager needs registry-mirror entry.
elliot: RBAC example for the keystore-reader role (for observability pods):`kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: keystore-observe
rules:
- apiGroups: ["keystore.redwood.io"]
  resources: ["auditlogs"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]`Bind only to `observability-sa` and limit verbs.
thomas: Runbook snippet: `if canary_fail_rate > 5% after 10m -> auto-rollback netpol changes; create SEV2 incident; attach canary report; kickstart dev patch for missing egress routes.`
maria: Action items: sanjay -> netpol manifests + allowlists; elliot -> Role/RoleBinding templates + token-audience enforcement; dina -> HSM failover SLA + signed-audit prototype; thomas -> IR runbook tweaks + auto-rollback thresholds; ryan -> proxy plan for bastion removal + cert-rotation steps; jen -> compliance checklist for logs. sync tomorrow 9am PT. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
